title: Start here
description: Set up your first game and choose your playing experience.

sections.title: About ZKMNEXT
paragraphs: ZKMNEXT GameSpace is an Android game launcher, device monitor and overlay toolkit. Project identity: ZKMNEXT · zuanvfx02. ZE2 v43f preserves Explore and adds the Expressive experience.
Features run on your device without a GameSpace account. System controls depend on Android, your ROM, chipset, kernel and granted access.

sections.title: Your first three steps
paragraphs: 1. Install the APK from a source you trust and open GameSpace. Android 10 / API 29 is the minimum requirement.
Complete the introduction, then try the Explore tour to discover the library, controls, monitor and Settings. Skip or replay it through Settings > Troubleshooting.
2. Add a game to your library. Choose Explore for everyday navigation, Handheld for a landscape lobby, or Gamepad for controller navigation.
3. Open access settings, grant the permissions your chosen features need, and launch a game from the library.

sections.title: Before tuning
paragraphs: Start with Basic access and the Balance profile. Check game detection and overlays before enabling kernel or charging controls.
A visible feature label does not guarantee hardware support. Read compatibility results and operation messages.

title: Expressive experience
description: A livelier introduction, your first Explore tour, and a more measured Energy Cube.

sections.title: A familiar introduction
paragraphs: ZKMNEXT and Game Space remain at the center of the introduction. A vector cube assembles in stages, pages move with Next and Back, and step indicators transition smoothly. Existing access, permission and privacy choices remain available.
Additional motion becomes static when system animations are disabled or battery saver is active. Existing users are not forced through setup again.

sections.title: Try the Explore tour
paragraphs: After first-time setup, follow the guide card at the bottom of the screen. Next visits the actual Home, App list, Customization, Monitoring and Settings pages. Add a game opens the real app picker.
The card reserves its own space instead of covering page controls. Use Back to return or close the card to skip. Progress is saved, and finishing returns you to Home.
Replay it through Settings > Troubleshooting > Replay Explore tour. The tour never enables Root, shell access or device permissions automatically.

sections.title: Energy Cube rendering budgets
paragraphs: Decorative Energy Cube and v2 rendering is capped at 60 fps; MID and LITE devices retain a 30 fps budget. Energy Cube v2 shares one clock between the scene and slow-frame detection, and caches text measurements until the text changes.
Explore ambient motion stops when the screen is not visible. These UI budgets reduce repeated rendering work; they do not guarantee higher game FPS.

sections.title: Documentation for your next session
paragraphs: Find guides from the home page, compare three modes, and follow system signals on the interactive map. Search runs locally in your browser; open it with Ctrl or Command K.
Articles include a mobile table of contents and a Copy link button. Theme and reduced motion follow your device preferences.

title: Meet ZEA
description: The official anime character and companion of ZKMNEXT GameSpace, in Void and Mini forms.

sections.title: GameSpace's own character
paragraphs: ZEA is the official anime character of ZKMNEXT GameSpace. She is the face and companion of your gaming space, with ZEA Void for the Character Room and ZEA Mini as your on-screen assistant.

sections.title: Void and Mini
paragraphs: Void Vanguard, Gothic Void, Crimson Reaper and Frost Void are ZEA's four outfits. Explore expressions, poses, actions and equipment in the Character Studio.
Void and Mini are two forms of the same character. Matching outfit and equipment IDs let compatible appearance choices follow both forms.

sections.title: Bring ZEA into the app
paragraphs: Open Virtual Character > Archive and import Zea-Void.zip and Zea-Void-Mini.zip. Select the full-size pack for the room and Mini for the assistant. Character artwork comes from imported packs.
MTP dialogs that use a character display the selected assistant. Character and dialog settings remain available in Character Studio and MTP studio.

sections.title: View the previews
paragraphs: The website home page features official ZEA artwork and actual Character Room, Dressing Room and Action Stage previews. All character previews use the latest ZEA Void packs.

title: What's new in ZE2 v43f
description: An Expressive introduction, the first Explore tour, Energy Cube improvements and a new docs website.

sections.title: The Expressive experience
paragraphs: The introduction retains ZKMNEXT's identity with a vector Energy Cube, layered page transitions and animated step indicators. The Explore tour opens real app pages and can be replayed from Troubleshooting.

Energy Cube caps decorative rendering. Version 2 caches text measurements and uses one frame clock. The docs website adds a new landing page, keyboard-accessible mode tabs and a clearer reading experience.

sections.title: Input plugins work together
paragraphs: Keymap, Shoulder Triggers, Gravity X and Macro playback share one touch session. Each plugin holds its own lease, so stopping one does not stop the others.
TouchLanes assigns local finger IDs to 32 physical lanes. Keymap buttons and Macro fingers no longer overwrite each other.

Recording a macro still requires raw touchscreen capture. If a mapper owns the screen, GameSpace shows a message instead of recording empty data. The sensitivity wheel cannot run alongside touch mapping yet.

sections.title: Scout shuts down completely
paragraphs: ScoutGuard records system settings before Scout changes them. GameSpace restores them when you disable Scout and when the app opens again.
If you force-stop the app, the Root process or shell server runs the recovery script previously registered by ScoutGuard.
Accessibility services you enabled yourself stay enabled. GameSpace only detaches services that Scout enabled through Root or Shizuku.

sections.title: A tidier Gravity X
paragraphs: Each Gravity X screen has a Minimize action. Its window becomes a draggable bubble while touch and gamepad input continue reaching the game.
Drag the editor toolbar using its left handle or collapse it into one row. Mapping buttons stay above the toolbar and remain reachable.

sections.title: Lighter overlays
paragraphs: Hidden overlays stop drawing. FPS sampling and telemetry pause while the screen is off.
Macro path overlays animate only during playback. In Shizuku or Axeron mode, sensor readers use the GameSpace server when it is active.
These are source-level changes. Results still depend on Android, your ROM and available access; test them on your device.

title: Access and permissions
description: Basic, Shizuku/Axeron and Root provide different capabilities.

sections.title: Choose your access level
paragraphs: Basic supports the library, statistics, profiles, music and UI features. Overlays still require display-over-other-apps permission.
Shizuku / Axeron execute shell commands under the service's UID. An ADB-based service does not automatically have Root privileges.
Root enables kernel controls exposed by the device. It cannot create missing charging, fan or governor interfaces.

sections.title: Permissions by feature
paragraphs: Usage access detects foreground games and records playtime. Overlay access enables panels, FPS, crosshairs and anti-mistouch zones. Regular notifications provide foreground-service status and controls.
Notification access supports Barrage, compatible call popups and Device Auto music. You can disable Barrage while continuing to use Device Auto.
DND access controls interruption settings. Supported magnification features use Accessibility, separately from Root/ADB access. Music files are selected through Android's document picker.

sections.title: If access is disconnected
paragraphs: Start Shizuku/Axeron and grant GameSpace permission. Select the correct backend, check its UID and status, then run the compatibility test again.
ADB access may need reactivation after a restart. Battery-optimization exemptions can help keep services running, but behavior varies by ROM.

title: Explore: Material 3 Expressive
description: Five focused destinations and one direct tuning dashboard.

sections.title: Five destinations
paragraphs: Home, Apps, Customization, Monitor and Settings retain their latest structure. Home, library and monitoring layouts are preserved.

sections.title: Compact customization
paragraphs: Performance profile and boost, paired Refresh rate and Render engine tiles, then grouped rows for additional tuning, focus, power/temperature and session extras. Simple values use selection dialogs. Complex controls open a direct one-step editor with the matching appbar title and Back action. Default and per-game tuning keep their existing stores.

sections.title: Mode separation
paragraphs: Console-only features remain in Handheld. Virtual-floating enablement stays on the overview and its report/test has one diagnostic detail. Game icon wallpaper remains retired. Imported wallpapers, existing feature engines and user data are preserved.

sections.title: Expressive, quieter styling
paragraphs: v8.46 uses Material 3 1.5.0-beta02, released 21 October 2026 (stable remains 1.4.0). Explore has its own expressive theme/motion, native interactive and checked settings lists, connected profile/Monitor choices and shape-morphing navigation/Apps controls. Home is more restrained, with a solid tonal banner and quieter default surfaces. Existing features, navigation and stores are retained.

title: Explore, Handheld and Gamepad
description: One library, three ways to navigate.

sections.title: Explore
paragraphs: Explore has five destinations: Home, Apps, Customization, Monitor and Settings. Home provides your library and session entry points; gaming controls are grouped in Customization. Ultra Smooth remains available in Settings.
Search opens the same settings pages. Manage per-app profiles and profile transfers through Apps.

sections.title: Handheld
paragraphs: The landscape lobby brings together your library, quick controls, wallpapers, decorations and profile. Add a game, select it and choose Start.
Floating Wallpaper can be disabled or use Orbit, Starflight, Alien and Crystal. Backdrops, particles, vignette and personal images are configured separately.

sections.title: Gamepad
paragraphs: Console mode provides controller input, visible focus and on-screen button hints. Glyphs follow the detected controller; test the actual mapping with your own device.
Use the directional buttons or stick to navigate, then follow the legend to select or go back. Android manages pairing and input devices.

title: In-game overlays
description: Choose a panel that fits your screen and playing habits.

sections.title: Energy Cube
paragraphs: A two-sided panel displays telemetry and controls. The v8.26 layout constrains its viewport by both width and height, preserving proportions and centering the panel vertically on squarer screens.
Screens with 4:3 or 16:10 ratios may have space above and below the panel. This keeps its sides from colliding. Tablet layout changes still require physical-device testing.

sections.title: Compact
paragraphs: A side panel with a scrollable vertical rail. Home contains telemetry and a mini player. The menu separates Perform, Display, Charging, Connect, Aim, Tools, Kernel, Widgets and Apps.
Perform includes Actions/Auto and preload. Display contains Screen/Render/Color. Charging contains bypass and device setup. Kernel provides CPU/GPU, scheduler and advanced controls.
Colors follow the Energy Cube profile: green for Balance, red for Rise and cyan for Eco. Sizing accounts for padding, handles and window space; vertical position uses the measured panel height.

sections.title: Controls and limits
paragraphs: Long panels, rails and pages support scrolling. Adjust dock side and size in settings, and close a panel if it obstructs game controls.
Very small screens can still produce small controls. Valid geometry alone does not guarantee readability, touch-target size or freedom from system-gesture conflicts.

title: Profiles and automation
description: Understand CPU profiles and Android game boost.

sections.title: Eco, Balance and Rise
paragraphs: Eco limits load where supported. Balance is the starting point for everyday use. Rise requests higher performance within your access and hardware capabilities.
Android Game boost controls the system game mode, separately from CPU profiles. A ROM or game may ignore the request. Higher FPS is not guaranteed.

sections.title: Automatic control and temperature
paragraphs: Auto can select a profile when a game session starts, react to low battery or screen-off, reduce the profile when hot and apply a timeout while a game is in the background.
The adaptive thermal controller reads available sensors and steps profiles down and back up. Sensor values vary by device. Keep manufacturer thermal protection enabled when starting out.

sections.title: Actions and preload
paragraphs: RAM cleaning, cache cleanup, restarting a game and fan controls serve different purposes. Fan controls work only on supported devices and interfaces.

Preload reads game files into cache within a budget. Its effect depends on your hardware and cache state; a larger budget does not guarantee better performance. Storage maintenance is separate from deleting cached files.

title: Display, rendering and color
description: Adjust your screen without mixing in kernel settings.

sections.title: Settings scope
paragraphs: Display settings can apply to all games by default or to one selected game. Check Apply settings to before changing values. Selecting a game in Display does not make kernel or charging controls per-game.

sections.title: Rendering and resolution
paragraphs: Render engine, resolution scale and FPS target depend on access and ROM support. HWUI does not control every native game engine. Requested FPS is not guaranteed FPS.
Some changes appear only after restarting the game. Follow Apply/Restart prompts. Optimize game uses profile compilation and may take time.

sections.title: Color
paragraphs: RGB and saturation controls depend on access. Reset restores neutral color through supported interfaces. Enable automatic per-game application only after checking the result.
Experimental renderer and SurfaceFlinger settings are not universal. Save your starting configuration and test one change at a time.

title: Charging and bypass
description: Power controls require real device support.

sections.title: What bypass means
paragraphs: Devices expose different charging switches. Disabling battery charging does not necessarily create a direct hardware power path to the system.
Charging has its own menu. Read candidate status and scan results; Root alone does not prove support.

sections.title: Scanning and restoration
paragraphs: Connect a charger and follow the battery requirements. The scan tests candidate controls and checks their results. It includes thresholds for releasing bypass and cancel/restore paths.
If restoration fails, stop experimenting, restore the required access and use Restore before another scan. Check actual charger behavior on your device.

sections.title: Validation limits
paragraphs: Low current alone is not proof of bypass. Temperature, load, cable quality and the charging controller can all change current readings.
The charging workflow has not been validated on every model. This documentation describes source behavior, not hardware certification.

title: Kernel and advanced controls
description: Governors, frequency limits and schedulers for each profile.

sections.title: Before making changes
paragraphs: Kernel settings require the right access and writable nodes. Run the compatibility test; ordinary permissions cannot make an unsupported feature available.
These settings are shared across games according to the selected profile. Deliberately choose the profile you intend to edit.

sections.title: Available controls
paragraphs: CPU/GPU governors, maximum CPU frequency, scheduler/I/O, top-app boost, tracing, priorities and chipset-specific options depend on detected capabilities.
The cluster editor provides minimum and maximum limits for detected clusters. These limits are separate from display FPS targets.

sections.title: Apply and Undo
paragraphs: Apply now requests application of your configuration. Undo/Restore uses the saved original values. Successful restoration still requires device access and permissions.
Treat value locking and experimental thermal controls carefully. Begin with defaults, change one option and check temperature and stability.

title: Music: two sources
description: Your ZKMNEXT playlist and media playing on your phone.

sections.title: ZKMNEXT playlist
paragraphs: Open Music, select ZKMNEXT and choose Add audio. The file picker supports importing multiple files. Files are not uploaded to a server.
The player supports play/pause, previous/next, seeking when duration is available, stop, loop and a floating music dot. Removing a playlist entry does not delete its original file.

sections.title: Device Auto
paragraphs: Select Device Auto and grant notification access if requested. Play music in an app or browser that provides an Android MediaSession.
GameSpace reads the title, artist, available artwork and playback state. Playing sessions take priority, and controls follow the actions provided by the source app.
Not every sound or website exposes a session. Missing detection is not a microphone-permission issue: this feature does not identify songs through microphone recordings.

sections.title: Mini player
paragraphs: Compact's Home mini player follows telemetry. Source selection is shared with widgets and the Music page. Changing the control source does not automatically start or stop another app's audio.
Disabled next/previous controls may indicate unsupported actions in the source app. If metadata is missing, check the session in Android's own media controls first.

title: Dashboard widgets
description: Choose the summaries and controls you actually need.

sections.title: Arrange your dashboard
paragraphs: Open Widgets and choose Customize. Select cards, use Up/Down to reorder them and choose Done. Choices and order are saved locally.
Cards can expand or collapse. FPS uses a primary number, CPU/GPU use paired meters and other controls can be condensed to keep the panel readable.

sections.title: Available cards
paragraphs: Frame rate, CPU/GPU, Performance, brightness, volume, tools, focus/alerts, monitor, crosshair, color, network, battery/thermal, quick settings and now playing.
Performance/Color/Charging shortcuts open their matching configuration category instead of duplicate editors. Read unavailable values as unavailable, rather than zero performance.

title: Controllers, macros and aiming
description: Console navigation and input tools while you play.

sections.title: Controllers
paragraphs: Pair a controller through Android, then open Gamepad mode. GameSpace detects input devices and adapts the on-screen button legend.
Navigation support in GameSpace does not guarantee support in a particular game. For unrecognized devices, compare the buttons with the legend and test manually.

sections.title: Macros and touch tools
paragraphs: Macro recording, floating controls, path markers, shoulder triggers, the sensitivity wheel, hold/double-tap and image-match triggers depend on permissions and access.

Shoulder Triggers, Keymap, Gravity X and Macro playback share one touch session. Capture combines real fingers with mapped input. If unavailable, a C++ kernel fallback tries free slots on the same touchscreen node. If both paths are rejected, activation reports the reason instead of enabling a mode that cancels analog input. Kernel support depends on drivers and ROM permissions. The documented Android 16 device configuration has not been physically tested. Existing F1/F2 Shoulder settings are retained.

Macro playback keeps one session across loops, preserves hold/drag timing and supports 0.25–4× speed in Keylink and floating controls. Stop waits for contact cleanup. Since v25 it can run alongside Keymap, Shoulder and Gravity X. Recording still needs raw touchscreen access: pause the mapper that owns it first. Enable the tool before holding the analog control. Rotation or access changes stop playback.
Image-match tools use the reference image and region you select; they are not an AI model that understands a game. Rotation and resolution changes can alter coordinates.
Some games prohibit input automation. Check the game's rules before enabling macros.

sections.title: Crosshair and Scout
paragraphs: Crosshair is an overlay; adjust its appearance and position without changing game assets. Scout uses supported Android magnification. Since v25, disabling Scout closes its lens, restores magnification settings and detaches only accessibility services it enabled, including after a force-stop.
Move or disable an overlay if it blocks buttons. Test one input tool at a time when first setting up.

title: Barrage, focus and anti-mistouch
description: Control interruptions with clear choices.

sections.title: Barrage and bubbles
paragraphs: Grant notification access, select source apps and enable Barrage. Ten styles are available: Starlight, Neon Pulse, Royal Crest, Cyber HUD, Arcade Pop, Inferno, Frost Byte, Sakura Bloom, Toxic Core and Obsidian.
Adjust speed, position, font, opacity, character limit and quick reply. Long messages are limited to three lines with an ellipsis. Previews and notifications use the same bubble builder.

sections.title: Focus and calls
paragraphs: DND, heads-up blocking and call popups are separate controls. Some operations require DND access or shell access. Quick reply is available only when a notification provides a compatible reply action.

sections.title: Edge protection
paragraphs: Preview corner zones through Game Center > System anti mistouch. During play, these zones are transparent but still capture touch.

Choose Small/Medium/Broad Range. If game buttons become difficult to press, reduce or disable the zone through settings or the session notification. System navigation gestures can still take priority.

title: Wallpapers, decorations and profiles
description: Personalize your space without changing system access.

sections.title: Wallpapers and atmosphere
paragraphs: Game space wallpaper includes backdrops, personal images, dimming, particles, vignette and Floating Wallpaper. Floating Wallpaper can be toggled independently, including with an AMOLED background.
Orbit preserves the original planets. Starflight uses rockets and satellites, Alien uses saucers and moons, and Crystal uses crystal shapes. Decorative objects do not capture touch input.

sections.title: Themes and profiles
paragraphs: Palette, AMOLED, scale and blur follow the relevant appearance settings. Compact continues to use performance-profile colors.
User profiles support an avatar, banner, decorations, name and statistics based on local usage. Per-game wallpapers can use available artwork.

sections.title: Animated wallpapers and rewards · v8.32
paragraphs: Handheld and Gamepad support photos, animated GIFs and muted looping videos up to 150 MiB. Select media in Game space wallpaper. Floating objects animate in both modes.
Common Android Motion Photos with embedded MP4 metadata are recognized. Other Live Photos require exporting and selecting the video. Codec support depends on your device.

Profiles include 20 achievements and free reward capsules. Each achievement grants one lifetime ticket and its direct decoration reward. Capsules grant a new permanent collection item with equal probability among remaining capsule items. Rune Circle has been removed.

title: Monitoring and services
description: Understand where readings come from and how sessions behave.

sections.title: Telemetry
paragraphs: CPU/GPU frequency and load, RAM, battery, temperature, refresh rate, network and FPS use readers supported by the device. GPU load may be estimated; read the indicator.
Display refresh rate is not game FPS. Ping to 1.1.1.1 indicates internet connectivity, not game-server latency. Traffic readings generally cover the whole device.

sections.title: Android services
paragraphs: Foreground services maintain game detection, overlays, music and enabled tools. Most internal services are not exported. Notification and accessibility services use Android binding permissions.
Closing a game, locking the screen, stopping a service or revoking access should follow the available cleanup/recovery paths. A ROM may stop services despite requested battery exemptions.

sections.title: Testing status
paragraphs: The source includes cleanup, sampling limits and recovery. That alone does not establish battery use, long-term stability or recovery on every ROM.
An error-free UI does not prove backend behavior. Test session start/end, rotation, lock/unlock, access loss and recovery after process termination.

title: Data, backups and recovery
description: Keep local backups under your control.

sections.title: Storage
paragraphs: Settings and layouts use SharedPreferences; other data uses local files/JSON. Core features do not require a server database. Automatic Android backup is disabled in the manifest.
Clearing app data or uninstalling can erase profiles, notes and statistics. Save a manual backup when needed.

sections.title: Export and import
paragraphs: Use Game Center's Backup/Restore. A settings backup does not automatically include original music or wallpaper files. Keep media separately.
Restoration across preference files is not one global transaction; failures can leave partial results. Check important settings after import.

sections.title: Diagnostics
paragraphs: Crash/event logs are stored locally for diagnosis. Read reports and redact information you do not want to share before sending them.
Local logs do not imply automatic crash uploads.

sections.title: Capsule progress · v8.32
paragraphs: Full backups include permanent capsule collections and spent achievement-ticket IDs. Restore preserves the union with newer local progress; repeatedly importing an old backup does not replenish spent tickets.
Keep recent backups before moving devices. An older backup cannot recover later events. Wallpaper media is private but not embedded in configuration backups; keep the original file separately.

title: Privacy and connections
description: Local data, permissions and network activity explained.

sections.title: Data on your device
paragraphs: GameSpace does not provide an account or cloud backend for library/settings. Profiles, layouts, music choices, playtime and diagnostic logs are managed locally by the reviewed implementation.
Notification access is sensitive: enable it only for features you use. Source apps and Android control available media metadata.

sections.title: Existing connections
paragraphs: The updater contacts GitHub over HTTPS. Ping measurements contact 1.1.1.1 when network/latency tools are active, so the app is not entirely offline.
Destination servers can see your IP address. Music-app and browser providers' policies also apply when you use their services.

sections.title: This documentation website
paragraphs: The static documentation UI has no analytics, ads, external fonts or application database. Search runs in your browser, and theme preferences use localStorage when available. Hosting access settings may require visitors to sign in.
The hosting provider may record network requests under its own policies. A static website does not guarantee the absence of server access logs.

sections.title: GitHub profiles and external links
paragraphs: About requests public maintainer/contributor information from the GitHub API and avatars from GitHub hosting. Public metadata is cached locally. Endpoint providers can see your IP address.
Community and donation links open external apps or browsers under their own privacy policies. Messages and donations are never submitted automatically.

title: Building and repository structure
description: Developer setup and the project's build workflow.

sections.title: Toolchain
paragraphs: Use JDK 21 and the Android SDK/build tools selected by the project. The supplied source uses SDK 37 with its configured minor API level and Build Tools 37.0.0. Minimum Android API is 29; target SDK is selected in app/build.gradle.kts. Read plugin and wrapper versions from the repository.
Run bash gradlew :app:assembleDebug for a development APK and bash gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest for unit tests. Debug output is in app/build/outputs/apk/debug/.

sections.title: Delivery baseline
paragraphs: Release and native-backend configuration remain in the source. Follow the existing build workflow for its CMake, NDK and Rust requirements. Documentation revisions are not APK version numbers.
UI/JVM compilation and targeted tests do not replace a complete native release build or physical-device testing. Read the validation notes for the checks actually performed.

sections.title: Source map
paragraphs: app/src/main/kotlin/com/zkmnext/gamespace/feature/gamespace contains UI, overlays, session tools, music and Game Center. Its tune subdirectory contains tuning engines and configuration.

library/device contains monitoring/input/usage, library/shell contains access backends, and core contains compatibility, diagnostics, updates and modes. Run app/src/test and androidTest in their appropriate environments.

sections.title: Contributing
paragraphs: Read CONTRIBUTING.md. Keep changes focused, explain before/after behavior and report the tests actually run. Do not include tokens, passwords, private media or sensitive logs.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Identify the symptom, check access and test one change.

sections.title: An overlay is missing
paragraphs: Check display-over-other-apps permission, game detection, the game library and service notifications. Some ROMs restrict overlays on certain screens.
If a panel is stuck near an edge, change its dock or reopen it after rotation. Test without other tools to distinguish input problems from layout issues.

sections.title: Music is not detected
paragraphs: Select Device Auto and grant notification access. Play a track and check whether Android itself shows media controls. Detection cannot be guaranteed for apps or websites without a MediaSession.

sections.title: Zero FPS or missing sensors
paragraphs: Check the FPS backend and access rights. The foreground game must be detected. Some sensors are not exposed by the ROM; missing readings should not be replaced by unlabeled estimates.

sections.title: Controller or macro issues
paragraphs: Test the controller using Android's input-device settings. Check Gamepad mode and its legend. For macros, adjust coordinates after rotation or resolution changes and verify access requirements.

sections.title: Heat, charging and lost access
paragraphs: Return to defaults/Balance, stop experimenting, then check restoration and access. Do not keep increasing boost when temperatures are already rising.
For bug reports, include app version, Android/ROM, device model, access mode, reproduction steps and expected behavior. Sensor and charging behavior must be checked on real hardware.

title: FAQ and support status
description: Straight answers about supported behavior.

sections.title: Is Root required?
paragraphs: Not for basic features. Some tools require shell or Root, and some also need compatible hardware or kernel interfaces.

sections.title: Does it run on iPad?
paragraphs: This is an Android app. Tablet/iPad-ratio references describe shapes such as 4:3 on Android devices, not iPadOS support.

sections.title: Is tablet support guaranteed?
paragraphs: No. The v8.26 changes improve viewport calculations and panel positioning. Source and geometry checks do not replace rendering, touch, cutout and rotation tests on tablets.

sections.title: Can I download an APK here?
paragraphs: This website documents the source. Source packages are not installable APKs. Use the owner's published GitHub Releases for available builds.

sections.title: Licensing and ownership
paragraphs: The project is ZKMNEXT, maintained by zuanvfx02. Source licensing is stated in LICENSE; supporting components retain their documented third-party terms and notices.
This documentation does not claim bug-free operation, universal compatibility or that every third-party library is original ZKMNEXT code.
